title: subqueries, written different ways, and the plans they become

steps.sql:
SELECT count(*) FROM customers
WHERE id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE status = 'refunded')
steps.note: IN becomes a semi join: the refunded orders' customer ids are de-duplicated, then joined to customers.

steps.sql:
SELECT count(*) FROM customers
WHERE id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE status = 'refunded')
steps.note: IN | refunded

steps.sql:
SELECT count(*) FROM customers AS c
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders AS o
              WHERE o.customer_id = c.id AND o.status = 'refunded')
steps.note: EXISTS with a correlated condition: pulled up into the same semi join, the same plan.

steps.sql:
SELECT count(*) FROM customers AS c
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders AS o
              WHERE o.customer_id = c.id AND o.status = 'refunded')
steps.note: EXISTS | refunded

steps.sql:
SELECT count(*) FROM customers
WHERE id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders)
steps.note: with all 10,000 orders on the inner side, the same idea: 10,000 customer ids de-duplicated to 1,962, then joined.

steps.sql:
SELECT count(*) FROM customers
WHERE id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders)
steps.note: IN | any order

steps.sql:
SELECT count(*) FROM customers AS c
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders AS o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id)
steps.note: and EXISTS lands on the same plan again.

steps.sql:
SELECT count(*) FROM customers AS c
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders AS o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id)
steps.note: EXISTS | any order

steps.sql:
SELECT count(*) FROM customers
WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders)
steps.note: NOT IN can't become an anti join (a NULL in the subquery would change the answer), so it stays a SubPlan: hashed, built once.

steps.sql:
SELECT count(*) FROM customers
WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders)
steps.note: NOT IN | 4MB

steps.sql:
SELECT count(*) FROM customers AS c
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders AS o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id)
steps.note: NOT EXISTS becomes an anti join.

steps.sql:
SELECT count(*) FROM customers AS c
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders AS o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id)
steps.note: NOT EXISTS | 4MB

steps.sql: SET work_mem = '64kB'
steps.note: shrink work_mem so the hashed SubPlan doesn't fit.

steps.sql:
SELECT count(*) FROM customers
WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders)
steps.note: with work_mem too small for the hash table, NOT IN becomes a plain SubPlan: the materialized orders are scanned again for every customer.

steps.sql:
SELECT count(*) FROM customers
WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders)
steps.note: NOT IN | 64kB

steps.sql:
SELECT count(*) FROM customers AS c
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders AS o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id)
steps.note: the anti join doesn't care much: it adapts its join method.

steps.sql:
SELECT count(*) FROM customers AS c
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders AS o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id)
steps.note: NOT EXISTS | 64kB

steps.sql: RESET work_mem
steps.note: back to the default.

steps.sql:
WITH fr AS (SELECT id, name, city FROM customers WHERE country = 'FR')
SELECT count(*) FROM fr WHERE city = 'Paris'
steps.note: a CTE used once is inlined: both conditions end up on one scan of customers.

steps.sql:
WITH fr AS (SELECT id, name, city FROM customers WHERE country = 'FR')
SELECT count(*) FROM fr WHERE city = 'Paris'
steps.note: inlined

steps.sql:
WITH fr AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT id, name, city FROM customers WHERE country = 'FR')
SELECT count(*) FROM fr WHERE city = 'Paris'
steps.note: MATERIALIZED keeps it separate: the CTE runs first, and the outer filter runs on its result.

steps.sql:
WITH fr AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT id, name, city FROM customers WHERE country = 'FR')
SELECT count(*) FROM fr WHERE city = 'Paris'
steps.note: MATERIALIZED

steps.sql:
SELECT count(*)
FROM (SELECT id, name, city FROM customers WHERE country = 'FR' OFFSET 0) AS fr
WHERE city = 'Paris'
steps.note: OFFSET 0 is the old trick for the same thing: a subquery with a LIMIT or OFFSET can't be pulled up.

steps.sql:
SELECT count(*)
FROM (SELECT id, name, city FROM customers WHERE country = 'FR' OFFSET 0) AS fr
WHERE city = 'Paris'
steps.note: OFFSET 0

steps.sql:
SELECT c.name, (SELECT count(*) FROM orders AS o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id) AS orders
FROM customers AS c
WHERE c.city = 'Paris'
ORDER BY c.id
steps.note: a correlated scalar subquery in SELECT is a SubPlan, run once per outer row: 66 scans of orders.

steps.sql:
SELECT c.name, (SELECT count(*) FROM orders AS o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id) AS orders
FROM customers AS c
WHERE c.city = 'Paris'
ORDER BY c.id
steps.note: scalar
